NABTARA

We are a multidisciplinary innovation team developing FieldWise, an AI-powered platform for climate-resilient agriculture. Using NASA Earth observation data, we analyze climate conditions, estimate crop water requirements, and compare crop rotation strategies. Our platform identifies shifting decisions, explores alternatives under water scarcity, and explains the evidence behind each recommendation.

Our mission: Transforming space data into smarter, more sustainable farming

NABTARA | From Space Data to Agricultural Decisions

NABTARA is an AI-assisted agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers in arid regions make smarter crop rotation and water management decisions using NASA Earth observation data.

Farmers enter their location, farm area, preferred crops, and available water budget. The platform is also being developed to integrate GPM precipitation, SMAP soil moisture, and HLS vegetation observations.

Our key innovation goes beyond traditional agricultural dashboards. The Decision Reversal Detector identifies when changing conditions alter the preferred agricultural decision. The Water Rescue Engine evaluates alternatives when water resources are insufficient, while the Evidence Confidence Engine communicates scientific uncertainty and data limitations.

A multilingual Gemini-powered assistant makes complex findings easier for farmers to understand, while scientific calculations remain independently implemented.
Developed using Madinah, Saudi Arabia, as an initial case study, NABTARA transforms satellite observations into practical, transparent agricultural decisions.
Our mission is to make space-based knowledge accessible, actionable, and valuable for sustainable agriculture.
details:
NABTARA | From Space Data to Agricultural Decisions

Project Overview

NABTARA is a multilingual, AI-assisted agricultural decision-support platform developed to address one of the most pressing challenges facing farmers in arid environments: making reliable crop-planning decisions under limited water availability and changing climate conditions.

Developed using Madinah, Saudi Arabia, as an initial case study, NABTARA transforms Earth observation data into actionable agricultural insights.

How It Works

Farmers enter their farm location, cultivated area, preferred crops, and available water budget.

The platform retrieves NASA POWER climate data and uses the internationally recognized FAO-56 Penman–Monteith methodology to calculate reference evapotranspiration (ET0), estimate crop water requirements, and compare alternative crop rotations.

NASA GPM precipitation data are also part of our data integration workflow. Additional integration work targets NASA SMAP soil moisture and Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) vegetation observations. These satellite components are subject to data availability, retrieval verification, and quality assessment.

The resulting analysis helps farmers evaluate water demand, crop suitability, climate-related constraints, and alternative agricultural scenarios.

Innovation and Creativity

NABTARA goes beyond displaying satellite observations through five complementary capabilities:

1. Decision Reversal Detector: Identifies when changing environmental conditions alter the preferred agricultural option and distinguishes ranking changes from water-budget feasibility changes.

2. Water Rescue Engine: Detects water deficits and explores mitigation strategies, including reducing cultivated area, adjusting crop selection, and improving irrigation efficiency.

3. Evidence Confidence Engine: Communicates data quality, missing observations, model assumptions, and scientific limitations.

4. Interactive Scenario Laboratory: Allows farmers to explore different crop rotations, water budgets, and climatic conditions before implementation.

5. Gemini AI Assistant: Explains scientific results in accessible language while keeping mathematical calculations within independently implemented scientific engines.

For example, if all proposed crop rotations require more water than a farmer’s available budget, NABTARA does not simply recommend the least water-intensive option. It identifies that none of the options is currently feasible, estimates the water deficit, and explores alternatives.

Technology and Development

NABTARA was developed using:

  • TypeScript and JavaScript
  • React and Vite for the user interface
  • Node.js and Express for backend services
  • Firebase Authentication and Firestore for user and farm-data management
  • IndexedDB for local browser storage
  • Google Gemini API for AI-assisted explanations
  • NASA data services and APIs for Earth observation integration
  • FAO-56 scientific equations and custom agricultural decision engines

The platform supports Arabic, English, Spanish, Urdu, Persian, and Hindi, with responsive interfaces for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

The current prototype is software-based and does not require dedicated hardware.

Scientific Considerations and Data Transparency

Our design considers data provenance, unit conversion, missing observations, satellite spatial resolution, crop water requirements, irrigation efficiency, and uncertainty.

NABTARA uses authentic NASA climate observations where retrieval has been verified. Agricultural scenarios and predicted water demand are model-based estimates rather than direct field measurements.

Not all satellite integrations have completed live operational validation, and independent farm-level validation remains a future development priority.

Intended Impact

NABTARA aims to make space-derived knowledge accessible to farmers, researchers, and agricultural decision-makers.

By connecting climate observations with transparent crop-rotation and water-budget analysis, the platform seeks to support more informed agricultural planning, better management of scarce water resources, and improved climate adaptability.

Our long-term vision is to transform Earth observation data into practical, scientifically grounded decisions that contribute to more resilient and sustainable agriculture.
